name: Ahmad Jamal
hook: A jazz pianist famous for space and restraint, whose playing became a favourite source for hip-hop producers.
blurb: Ahmad Jamal was born in Pittsburgh in 1930 and became one of the most admired jazz pianists of his time. He was known for leaving space: playing fewer notes, repeating figures, and letting silence do some of the work, which suits a loop and is one reason hip-hop producers keep coming back to him. Miles Davis said he learned from him, and Davis's own accounts document it. Pete Rock sampled Jamal's 'I Love Music' for Nas's 'The World Is Yours' in 1994, and many other producers have used his records. He died in 2023, aged 92. Jazz is a roots lane on this map, traced only where a documented connection reaches later music, so Jamal is here as a much-sampled source (Q21).
